drug_class: NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug) combined with an acid reducer (H2 blocker)
purpose: This medication is used to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis. It combines a pain reliever (ibuprofen) with a stomach protector (famotidine) to help reduce the risk of stomach ulcers that ibuprofen can sometimes cause. It is typically used in adults who need long-term pain relief and are at risk for stomach problems.
how_it_works: Ibuprofen works by blocking chemicals in your body called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation. Famotidine works by reducing the amount of acid your stomach makes, which helps protect your stomach lining from the irritation that ibuprofen can cause. Together, they give you pain relief while being gentler on your stomach than taking ibuprofen alone.
common_side_effects: Nausea, upset stomach, heartburn, diarrhea, constipation, headache, dizziness, and gas are the most common side effects. Some people may also notice stomach pain or feel unusually tired.
warnings: This medication can increase the risk of heart attack or stroke, especially with long-term use or in people with heart disease. It can cause serious stomach or intestinal bleeding, sometimes without warning signs. Do not use it if you are pregnant, especially in the last trimester. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Tell your doctor if you have kidney, liver, or heart problems before taking it.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one tablet taken three times a day. It is best to take it with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same times each day and do not take more than prescribed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
